purpose: The data-driven table: pass `data` + `columns` and it renders the header, rows, selection, sorting, paging, empty / loading / error states and the footer `Pagination` itself, through the same `Table` parts (`Table.Header`, `Table.Row`, `Table.HeadCell`, `Table.Cell`), so its markup, tokens and accessibility are those of [`table`](./table.md). The headless **`@tanstack/vue-table`** engine lives here and only here: a hand-composed `Table` never loads it. A top **toolbar band** (`title` / `toolbar` / `filters` slots) sits above the scroll viewport for a title, the context-aware `Table.*` toolbar parts (search, filter, export, refresh, live) and removable filter chips; the `toolbar` and `filters` slots are scoped with the TanStack `table` instance so the consumer can drive filtering, global search and column visibility through the table's own methods. Pairs with [`Pagination`](./pagination.md) (rendered automatically in the footer when `paginated`). **Engine.** DataTable is driven by **`@tanstack/vue-table`** (`useVueTable` + `getCoreRowModel` / `getSortedRowModel` / `getFilteredRowModel` / `getPaginationRowModel`), covering sorting, pagination, row selection, column visibility, and global filtering — client- and server-side (`manualSorting` / `manualPagination` / `manualFiltering`). It is a pure-logic library (no markup/styles/positioning/animation), granted narrowly to the table family (this component and the editable `data-grid` that builds on it) per [`.claude/rules/dependencies.md`](../.claude/rules/dependencies.md) § Exceptions; rendering stays 100% in our primitives. State is exposed via v-model (`sorting`, `rowSelection`, `columnVisibility`, `globalFilter`, `pagination`, plus the structured `filters` model and the aggregate `state` snapshot below). `@tanstack/virtual` remains forbidden: the opt-in `virtual` mode windows the rows itself (spacer padding above and below the rendered slice, sized from a height index: each rendered row is measured with a `ResizeObserver`, rows not yet rendered take the average of the first rows measured, and when a row above the rows in view changes height the scroll position moves by the same amount so the rows in view stay still). Without `virtual`, a list of more than 200 rows renders its first 50 rows and mounts the rest as a spacer below them nears the viewport (an `IntersectionObserver`), so a long page costs what is on screen. **Toolbar & imperative API.** The toolbar band composes context-aware controls that drive the table through the injected context with no wiring: `Table.Filter` (the slot that hosts `FilterMenu` with `kind="menu"`, or `PropertyFilter` with `kind="property"`, over `filterFields`), `FilterMenu.Chips` with no `fields` in the `filters` slot (the applied fields of the menu kind), `CollectionPreferences` with no `columns` (visible columns and their order, written back on Confirm), `Table.Search` (the global text filter), `Table.Export` (CSV download), `Table.RefreshButton` and `Table.LiveButton`. Structured filters are a first-class model (`v-model:filters`, an `AppliedFilter[]` distinct from the free-text `globalFilter`) mapped to the TanStack column filters client-side, or emitted for a server refetch under `manualFiltering`. A `loading` prop renders skeleton rows for dynamic (server-side) data. The root exposes a **curated imperative API** via `defineExpose` (`reload`, `clearFilters`, `exportCsv`, `getState`, `setState`) so controls or logic outside the table can drive it through a template ref, and a serializable `TableStateSnapshot` (`sorting` / `pagination` / `columnVisibility` / `columnOrder` / `globalFilter` / `filters`) is exposed via `v-model:state` + `getState()` / `setState()` + an `initialState` seed — the component stays router-agnostic, so the consuming app owns any URL / localStorage persistence. CSV serialization lives in a pure util at [`@aziontech/webkit/utils/csv`](../packages/webkit/src/utils/csv.ts) (`toCsv` + `downloadCsv`). **Types** (declared in `injection-key.ts`, re-exported for consumers): `FilterOperator` = `'eq' | 'neq' | 'contains' | 'not-contains' | 'starts-with' | 'ends-with' | 'gt' | 'gte' | 'lt' | 'lte' | 'in' | 'not-in' | 'is-empty' | 'is-not-empty' | 'within' | 'between'` (`within` holds a period id — `24h`, `7d`, `30d`, `3m` — and matches dates inside that window ending now; `between` holds `[start, end]` epoch milliseconds, either one `''` for an open bound; both read the cell as a `Date`, a timestamp or a parseable date string); `TableFilterKind` = `'menu' | 'property'`; `FilterField` = `{ id: string; label: string; type: 'text' | 'number' | 'select' | 'multi-select' | 'boolean' | 'date'; operators?: FilterOperator[]; options?: { label: string; value: string | number | boolean }[] }`; `AppliedFilter` = `{ field: string; operator: FilterOperator; value: string | number | boolean | Array<string | number>; label?: string }`; `TableStateSnapshot` = `{ sorting?: SortingState; pagination?: PaginationState; columnVisibility?: VisibilityState; columnOrder?: string[]; globalFilter?: string; filters?: AppliedFilter[] }` (every field optional so `setState` / `initialState` accept a partial; JSON-serializable). **Collections.** `useCollection` (`@aziontech/webkit/use-collection`) drives DataTable in both client and server modes: `tableProps` binds `data` (one page), `columns` (ordered by the saved preferences), `rowKey`, `loading`, `sorting`, `manualSorting` / `manualFiltering` / `manualPagination`, `paginated`, `pagination`, `rowCount`, `pageSizeOptions`, `enableRowSelection`, `rowSelection`, `columnVisibility` and the three display preferences (`density`, `wrapLines`, `striped`) together with their update handlers, and `exportRows`, in one `v-bind`. The table keeps rendering one page; the composable owns filtering, sorting, paging and selection across pages, so `exportRows` hands `Table.Export` and `exportCsv()` every match rather than the page: in client mode the matching items (or every item for the `all` scope), in server mode what the collection's `exportAll` callback loads (the loaded page when there is none). **Cell presets and reordering.** The six `Table.Cell*` presets render the cells every list repeats, each inside a `#cell-<id>` slot: `Table.CellLink` (a name that leaves the screen: an optional muted leading glyph (`icon`) for the provider or resource type, a 12 px external mark, a tooltip naming the destination, underline on hover, no mark without a destination; optional `+N` overflow through `OverflowCount` and a copy button pinned to the end edge), `Table.CellId` (an identifier with its copy button), `Table.CellStatus` (one semantic `Tag`), `Table.CellTags` (as many tags as fit, the rest behind `+N`), `Table.CellTime` (avatar of the author plus a relative time that updates every minute, or counts from the nearest `WebkitProvider`'s `now`, the absolute time on the tooltip and for screen readers) and `Table.CellActions` (the row menu named after the row). `reorderable` adds a leading grip column: drag a grip with the pointer, or focus it and press Arrow Up, Arrow Down, Home or End; the table emits `update:data` with the reordered records and `reorder` with `{ from, to, row }`, announces every move in a polite status region and locks while a sort is applied; `rowReorderable` keeps chosen rows (a pinned default) in place.
useWhen: Use DataTable for records that share columns — any console list of resources people scan, sort and act on.

Records with the same fields shown in rows and columns, where the reader compares, sorts, selects or acts on rows (resource lists, logs, usage breakdowns): use DataTable for read-and-act lists of repeated records.
A list needs a toolbar for search, structured filters, column visibility, CSV export or refresh — the `Table.*` toolbar parts drive the DataTable through context.
Server-backed data that pages, sorts or filters on the API: `manual-pagination`, `manual-sorting` and `manual-filtering` emit the state instead of slicing locally.
Thousands of rows (`virtual`), tree rows (`get-sub-rows`), reorderable rows, infinite loading or a live tail.
avoidWhen: A small, static table or one whose cells need a layout the column model cannot express → compose it by hand with `table` (no engine in the bundle).
People edit many cells of many records in place, spreadsheet-style → use `data-grid`.
A short list of same-field rows added and removed inside a form (environment variables, headers) → use `attribute-editor`.
A short titled preview of a longer listing on a marketing page → use `listing-table`.
A feature-by-feature comparison of Azion with a competitor → use `comparison-table`.
Rows of mixed content (media, title, description, actions) that do not share columns → use `item`.
The same records as a grid of cards → use `cards` (same collection, card layout).
related: table` — the parts DataTable renders through, and the hand-composed table for small static content; its toolbar parts and cell presets go in DataTable's slots.
data-grid` — the editable, spreadsheet-like grid; use it when cells are edited in place.
pagination` — the page strip; a `paginated` DataTable renders and wires it in the footer.
listing-table` — marketing section that composes `table` for a linked preview of a list.
empty-state` — the pattern behind the table's default `empty` slot; override the slot for resource-specific copy and actions.
item` — list rows without a column structure.
filter-menu` — Use FilterMenu when people filter by picking known values per field (status, region, owner) and see them as chips — the default console list filter; `Table.Filter` hosts it by default.

property-filter` — Use PropertyFilter when people type queries with operators (Status = Active, Requests > 100) or free text they want to keep; `Table.Filter kind="property"` hosts it wired to the table (AND only).

collection-preferences` — Use CollectionPreferences for every 'how this list looks' setting: page size, visible and ordered columns, density, wrap; with no `columns` inside the toolbar it edits this table's columns.
bestPractices: For repeated data, pass `data` + `columns` and customize cells with the `cell-<columnId>` / `header-<columnId>` slots instead of composing N rows by hand. Compose `Table` by hand only for small, static tables.
Give rows a stable id under `row-key` (default `'id'`); selection and `v-model:row-selection` are keyed by it.
Mark the row-actions column `kind: 'action'` so it pins to the trailing edge; give chip or short-token columns a `minWidth` rather than a fixed `width`.

Give `Table.CellTime` dates from your data. Where the text must not depend on when it renders (an example, a test, a server render the browser hydrates), set `now` on the app's `WebkitProvider` and count sample dates back from that constant; never build them from `Date.now()` / `new Date()` in setup.
Drive loading through the `loading` prop (skeleton rows, `aria-busy`) and keep the `empty` slot for no-data copy — do not swap the table for a spinner.

On a phone a console list keeps its grid and scrolls sideways (the default). Set `stackable` only for a short list read one record at a time on a narrow, phone-first surface (a marketing listing, a summary in a side panel), where a card per row reads better than a scroll; never on a resource index, a log or a list compared across columns.

Type the rows, not the slot: pass a typed `data` (`ref<Domain[]>([])`, or a literal array) and destructure `#cell-name="{ row, value }"` — `row` is a `Domain` and `value` is `Domain['name']`. Keep a column's `id` equal to its `accessorKey` (or leave `id` out) so the typed `value` is the field the cell shows. Do not annotate the slot scope by hand or cast `row as Domain`; a wrong field (`row.nmae`) should be a type error.

Place `Table.Search`, `Table.Filter`, `CollectionPreferences`, `Table.Export` and `Table.RefreshButton` in the `toolbar` slot with no `v-model` wiring — they read the table from context. Import them from the `table` compound (`Table.Search`) or their own entries (`table-search`); the compound does not load the engine.
